object_owner.description: Owns every object. A NOLOGIN role no service connects as; migrations SET LOCAL ROLE into it and RESET before dbmate stamps the version.

app_runtime.description: The runtime identity permitted on app.* directly. Still policy-bound: the tables carry FORCE row-level security.

anon.description: The role an unauthenticated request becomes. Granted schema USAGE and nothing else.

authenticated.description: A request carrying a validated identity from Session 6 onward. Reads through api views, writes through the RPCs.

agent_writer.description: Agent identity permitted to call the write RPCs.

api_documentation.description: The role the OpenAPI capture and the documentation page read the published surface as. Holds view SELECT and EXECUTE on the write RPCs, which is what makes openapi-mode = follow-privileges publish the whole surface; the pre-request hook refuses it a request identity, so it can never perform what it advertises. Outputs schema v6, D158.

api_documentation_name.description: The same role, as a string literal rather than a quoted identifier, for the hook's `current_user::text = ...` comparison. Two placeholders over ONE source: they resolve from the same key in the same document, so they cannot name different roles -- which a second source, or a name written out beside the grant, could.

auth_service.description: The auth service's database identity. Session 6. Migration 0011 grants it schema USAGE and nothing else -- its LOGIN attribute, connection limit, SCRAM credential and statement_timeout are bootstrap-plane work, because anything ALTER ROLE is (D102), and the functions it will call arrive with the code that calls them.

project_admin.description: The administrator's request role, and a request role only from Session 6 Run 9: before that it existed, NOLOGIN and unreachable, because the authenticator held no membership in it. What it may do ADMINISTRATIVELY is not decided here or by the role name -- it is decided by the scope in the token, which is what API-ADMIN-001 states and why a project_admin without admin_users:write is refused. The membership is granted by the bootstrap plane (D266, D102); this placeholder exists so migration 0013 can give the role schema USAGE and the EXECUTE every request role needs to run the pre-request hook.

storage_service.description: The storage runtime's database identity. Session 7. The role has been in naming.ROLE_SUFFIXES since Session 3 as a NOLOGIN stub with a null verifier, so 0014 creates nothing and activates nothing (D307): its LOGIN attribute, connection limit, SCRAM credential and statement_timeout are bootstrap-plane work, because anything ALTER ROLE is (D102). This file grants it EXECUTE on seven SECURITY DEFINER functions and no privilege of any kind on app_private.storage_objects -- which is what makes 'the service cannot read another owner's row even by composing its own SQL' a property of the catalog rather than of the service's code.

migrations.name: schemas_and_default_privileges
migrations.description: The four schemas, pgvector in extensions rather than public, and a default-deny posture for function execution.

migrations.name: project_identity_and_ledger
migrations.description: The single-row identity sentinel that binds this volume to one project, and the ledger recording which bytes each version applied.

migrations.name: owner_scoped_tables_and_forced_rls
migrations.description: notes and tasks under FORCE row-level security, keyed on a transaction-local identity claim that denies when absent.

migrations.name: security_invoker_api_views
migrations.description: Read-only api views that run with the caller's authority, so the underlying row policy still applies.

migrations.name: write_rpcs
migrations.description: Two write functions that derive ownership from the request identity and take no owner parameter.

migrations.name: app_runtime_least_privilege
migrations.description: The application runtime role loses the direct reach into app and app_private that Session 3 granted it, default privileges included, and holds only what membership in authenticated carries. See SEC-DBX-002 and ADR 0041.

migrations.name: api_surface_convergence
migrations.description: ADR 0048: the catalog converges on the domain four documents froze. notes.body becomes content, tasks gains description and a bounded api.task_status derived from done, create_task is retired for update_task_status, and the api views and write RPCs are rebuilt over the result.

migrations.name: http_request_plane
migrations.description: app_private.postgrest_pre_request(), and the one private object an HTTP request role may reach: USAGE on app_private plus EXECUTE on that function, granted by name to anon and authenticated and to nothing else. See ADR 0052 and D138.

migrations.name: documentation_role
migrations.description: The documentation role's grants -- view SELECT plus EXECUTE on both write RPCs, which is what makes openapi-mode = follow-privileges publish the whole surface -- and the pre-request clause that refuses it a request identity, so the RPCs it advertises are ones it can never perform. See D158.

migrations.name: request_statement_timeout
migrations.description: The pre-request hook carries the request role's statement_timeout into the request transaction. PostgreSQL processes a role's settings only at login, and PostgREST reaches its request role with SET LOCAL ROLE -- so the timeouts ADR 0067 put on the roles bounded nothing. The value is still the document's; this reads what the bootstrap plane wrote and applies it for one transaction. See D198, ADR 0068.

migrations.name: identity_registry
migrations.description: The identity registry: app_private.users, user_credentials, agents, agent_credentials and auth_contract_state, plus the is_scope_set helper the scope columns are checked against. Created from nothing -- the runbook's 'extend the existing users table' has no subject, so every column is NOT NULL from creation and the backfill is struck rather than written over zero rows (D218). No foreign key reaches app.notes.owner_id: that column holds a claim value and ADR 0029 states in its title that it is trusted, not authenticated. auth_service is granted schema USAGE and nothing else; the functions it will call arrive with the code that calls them. See ADR 0078, D218, D228.

migrations.name: auth_access_plane
migrations.description: The access plane for human subjects: eight SECURITY DEFINER functions in app_private, granted to auth_service, which are the only way the service reaches the identity registry -- 0011 granted it schema USAGE and nothing else and said these would arrive with the code that calls them. Lookup is by the same normalised expression the unique index uses, and returns no row rather than raising for an unknown username, because the login path exists to make 'no such user' and 'wrong password' indistinguishable. auth_bootstrap_administrator takes a project-scoped pg_advisory_xact_lock derived from project_identity: measured, two concurrent callers without it both read 'no administrator' and both insert. It is NOT granted to auth_service -- a service that could call it is the public bootstrap endpoint that does not exist. The blanket REVOKE FROM PUBLIC is load-bearing rather than tidy: a new function is PUBLIC-executable by default and ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES records nothing for functions (D262). This is 0012 and Run 9's hook becomes 0013 (D261). See ADR 0084, D261, D262.

migrations.name: agent_plane_and_current_state_hook
migrations.description: The pre-request hook stops trusting a signature, and agents get the access plane 0012 gave humans. Until now the hook read `sub` and took the rest of the token on the strength of a valid signature; from here credential_version, authz_version, role and sorted scope are compared against current state inside the request's own transaction and any mismatch is refused -- which is what makes a disable, a password reset or a scope change take effect on the next request rather than at the next expiry (SEC-REV-001). The comparison goes through a SECURITY DEFINER helper returning a BOOLEAN over the whole claim tuple, never the subject's own values: a function answering 'what are X's scopes' would let any authenticated caller enumerate authority through a hook it cannot avoid running. project_admin becomes a request role and gets USAGE and EXECUTE; its authenticator MEMBERSHIP is the bootstrap plane's, not this file's (D266, D102). The agent roles stay ungranted, so an agent token fails at role switching before the hook runs. This is 0013 and the plan called it 0012 (D261). See D261, D266, D267.

migrations.name: object_storage_plane
migrations.description: The object-storage plane: app_private.storage_objects under a one-way pending -> available -> tombstoned state machine, storage_contract_state, and seven SECURITY DEFINER functions granted to storage_service and to nothing else. The service holds no privilege of any kind on the table, so a defect in it cannot read another owner's row even by composing its own SQL, and the proof attempts the read rather than asking has_table_privilege (D103). The download lookup answers absent, foreign, pending and tombstoned identically -- a caller that could tell them apart could enumerate another user's ids (STO-OWN-001), and that filter is the linearization point a committed tombstone precedes. Completion is a compare-and-set on state = pending, so it is idempotent and returns the current state rather than raising. The cleanup claim carries both halves of ADR 0104: the lease predicate is the correctness mechanism, because the provider DELETE happens outside the transaction and a row lock is released at COMMIT and at crash, and FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED is throughput only -- both measured on the locked pg18 digest with controls. Every CHECK was written against ADR 0080: a CHECK passes when its expression is NULL, so the coherence constraints are shaped to be total while the column checks are deliberately partial where the column is nullable. Does not touch the pre-request hook (D270). This is 0014 and the runbook called it 0012 (D312). See ADR 0104, D57, D262, D285, D307.

migrations.name: storage_completion_key
migrations.description: app_private.storage_completion_key(uuid, uuid) -- the one function 0014 needed and did not have. Completion must ask the provider how many bytes arrived before it moves an object to available, and to ask it needs the object's key; 0014 exposed the key only through storage_lookup_for_download (state = available) and storage_claim_cleanup_batch (state = tombstoned), so the pending state completion operates on was the one state with no reader. The alternative -- returning the key from storage_create_upload_intent and having the client hand it back -- is refused by STO-KEY-001, whose whole content is that no client-supplied key can reach a presign. This is 0015 and not an edit to 0014 because ADR 0091's three conditions were checked rather than assumed: no cluster holds 0014, but 0014 APPLIES perfectly well, and the ADR says in as many words that a migration which merely did the wrong thing does not qualify for in-place correction. The state predicate is pending OR available, not pending alone: the pending-only version broke idempotency (STO-COMPLETE-001), because a retried completion 404s before reaching the compare-and-set that makes it idempotent -- 0014's own comment calls that CAS idempotent, which was true of the function and false of the path through it. Tombstoned stays excluded, since completing one would resurrect it and the state machine is one-way. Owner and state are one predicate, so absent, foreign and tombstoned return zero rows alike (STO-OWN-001). EXECUTE to storage_service only, with an explicit REVOKE FROM PUBLIC beside the CREATE because a new function is PUBLIC-executable and ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES records nothing for functions (D57, re-measured as D262). Relies on the schema USAGE 0014 granted and does not re-grant it (D337). See ADR 0091, ADR 0104, D348.

migrations.name: storage_cleanup_write_window
migrations.description: app_private.storage_claim_cleanup_batch gains a fourth argument and the predicate 0014 was missing: an object is collectable only once nothing can still write to its key (ADR 0111). Found by writing the first caller for a plane released five runs earlier -- D348's shape a second time in one session. storage_tombstone moves a PENDING object deliberately, so that an abandoned intent is collectable without ever having been completed; but a pending object carries a presigned PUT minted for intent_expires_at, and a tombstone does not revoke it, because a presigned URL is a bearer credential and nothing in this system can withdraw one. 0014 would claim such an object one statement after the DELETE, delete an absent key at the provider, mark cleanup_completed_at, and never look at the row again -- so a write arriving on the still-live URL lands under a key nothing will ever collect, and section 4 forbids an orphan scan on the ground that a reconciler which lists and deletes untracked objects can delete data a human put there to recover something. Measured on the locked pg18 digest with two controls that came out the other way: an expired intent is claimed, and a completed object is claimed. The new clause is a disjunction and each side is a different argument -- completed_at IS NOT NULL means the key already holds bytes and a replayed PUT is refused 412 by the signed If-None-Match (Run 5, with the arm that matters being a caller who omits the header and gets 403 rather than an unconditional write), so waiting out the upload TTL would buy nothing; never completed means the key is empty and a presigned PUT would be a FIRST write, stopped only by the URL's own expiry, which is intent_expires_at by construction. p_write_grace_seconds is a parameter rather than a constant because its correct value is a fact about the provider's tolerance for a stale signature -- PostgREST was measured to allow 30 seconds where its documentation implies none (D241) -- and that measurement belongs beside the adapter that made it. A negative grace is refused rather than clamped, since clamping would hide exactly the bug it was asked about. The three-argument form is DROPPED rather than left as an overload: two functions answering which objects are collectable would be two authorities for one rule, and the old one is the version with the defect. Both halves of ADR 0104 are carried forward unchanged and this file was written from 0014's body rather than from memory of it (D270). This is 0016 and not an edit to 0014 because ADR 0091's condition 2 fails: 0014 applies perfectly well. EXECUTE to storage_service only, with an explicit REVOKE FROM PUBLIC (D57, D262) and RESET ROLE below the privileges block (D285). See ADR 0111, ADR 0104, ADR 0091, D348.

migrations.name: storage_verifier_subject_state
migrations.description: GRANT EXECUTE ON app_private.auth_user_state(uuid) TO storage_service -- the privilege ADR 0098's third verifier needs and was never given (D385). Found by the first host run of the storage surface: every authenticated request answered 500 Internal Server Error, plain text from Starlette's default handler because the exception escaped before the service's error middleware could shape it, and the cause was psycopg InsufficientPrivilege: permission denied for function auth_user_state. Thirteen deployment proofs failed on it with one cause. Storage runs the same AuthService.authenticate the auth service does, including the current-state comparison that makes a stale token useless (ADR 0095), and that comparison IS this function. Traced rather than assumed: authenticate calls exactly one repository method, state(user_id), so there is no second missing grant behind this one. 0012 created the access plane for its only caller at the time and granted the set to auth_service correctly; a second caller arrived in Session 7 and the grant did not move with it -- D333's question for the fifth time in one session, and D381's shape three runs earlier. No offline test could see it because nothing offline authenticates as storage_service against a real cluster; test_the_auth_role_can_execute_the_functions_the_service_calls does exactly the right thing for the auth role and had no storage twin, which Run 12 adds. ONE function, not the set: auth_service holds eleven here including auth_create_user, auth_set_password and auth_set_status, and storage verifies tokens rather than administering identities, so granting the set would hand a storage compromise the ability to mint and re-authorize subjects. No REVOKE FROM PUBLIC, because 0012 revoked it for this function and owns that privilege (D337); schema USAGE is 0014's. RESET ROLE below the privileges block (D285): GRANT EXECUTE requires ownership and the connected role on a host is migration_user, which owns nothing. This is 0017 and not an edit to 0012 because two clusters hold 0012 (ADR 0091). See ADR 0098, ADR 0113, ADR 0095, ADR 0091, D385, D381.

migrations.name: agent_read_plane
migrations.description: The agent read plane. app_private.agent_claims_are_current is 0013's auth_claims_are_current for agents, with one deliberate difference in the return type: it returns the agent's OWNER on a full tuple match and NULL otherwise, because an agent request runs under its owner's identity (ADR 0117) and the token does not carry it -- owner_id is uuid NOT NULL since 0011, so NULL means 'no agent matched' and nothing else. The pre-request hook gains one branch, discriminated on token_use rather than on current_user: branching on the physical role would work today because the authenticator's memberships happen to line up with the two registries, and that is the mechanism D393 was -- a boundary standing on a correlation. Run 1 measured an agent token and a human token carrying the same twelve claims, the same issuer, the same audience and the same key, so token_use is the only claim in the token minted to discriminate. credential_version must be 0 on the agent branch: D397 made 0 a value rather than an absence so that 'not a human' could be read, and the hook checks the convention instead of trusting it. The branch establishes app.user_id = the owner and app.agent_id = the agent, and NO POLICY MOVED: all eight owner policies from 0003 key on app.user_id, so an agent sees exactly the rows its owner sees. The hook was written from 0013's body rather than from memory of it (D270) and the diff is mechanical rather than claimed -- zero statement lines removed, twenty-one added, asserted by test_the_agent_branch_is_0013s_body_plus_a_branch. Two functions in api: mcp_agent_context, SECURITY DEFINER and taking NO argument so it can only describe the caller, returning zero rows for a non-agent rather than raising; and owner_activity_report, SECURITY INVOKER so the caller's own RLS bounds the counts -- a definer report would count every owner's rows and look correct until a second owner existed. It reads the api views rather than app.notes and app.tasks, because the API roles hold table SELECT without schema USAGE on app (0004), and counting rows must not widen that boundary. Both are granted to agent_reader only, and deliberately not to api_documentation, which is what keeps them out of the document follow-privileges builds as that role (ADR 0118); both are named under agent_rpcs in contracts/postgrest-api-surface.yaml, so ADR 0050's invariant holds -- nothing exists in api that the reviewed contract does not name. owner_activity_report is NOT granted to authenticated: the first draft granted it because AGT-READ-001 compares an agent's read against 'the equivalent PostgREST result' and a human who gets permission denied produces none, but a read RPC a human may call is a fifth human operation and ADR 0003's example domain is frozen. The equivalence is proved against the ROW surface instead, which is the stronger claim: two functions can be wrong in the same direction, a count that disagrees with the rows it counts cannot. BOTH comparison helpers are granted to all five request roles, and the first draft granted the agent helper to the agent role alone. Measured on the locked image, first run of the rig: a HUMAN token naming the agent role was refused with 'permission denied for function auth_claims_are_current' instead of AP401 -- correct outcome, false reason, D393 arriving through a missing grant. role and token_use are independent claims, so every combination of physical role and hook branch is reachable by a request. Measured across 23 arms with interleaved controls, applying all eighteen migrations as migration_user over TCP (dbmate's route, not psql -U postgres, which is the superuser route that let 0012 pass four sessions of green proofs while being unappliable -- D285) and making every request as the authenticator with SET ROLE (PostgREST's route; a privilege refusal measured as a superuser measures nothing, ADR 0065/0066). Targeted REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION ... FROM PUBLIC beside each of the three new functions rather than the blanket form (D57, re-measured as D262): a new function is EXECUTABLE BY PUBLIC the moment it exists, anon holds USAGE on schema api since 0001, and follow-privileges follows a PUBLIC grant. RESET ROLE below the privileges block (D285). This is 0018 and not an edit to 0013 because two clusters hold 0013 (ADR 0091). No role membership here: GRANT role TO role is bootstrap plane (D102, D266), and postgres-bootstrap.py grants the authenticator agent_reader with ADMIN FALSE, INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE. See ADR 0116, ADR 0117, ADR 0118, ADR 0052, ADR 0091.

migrations.name: agent_write_and_audit_plane
migrations.description: The agent write and audit plane. app_private.agent_audit is the durable attribution record ADR 0135 decides, and it is written by two SECURITY DEFINER functions in api called over PostgREST with the caller's own token, because the MCP runtime holds no database credential and must not gain one -- settings.load_mcp refuses to start if handed a signing key or any APG_DATABASE_* or APG_POOL_SIZE, and its zero share of the connection budget is a decision asserted by a test that parses the arithmetic (D407). Neither function takes a principal, an owner, a role or a scope: identity is read from the app.agent_id and app.user_id GUCs the pre-request hook set for this transaction, which is what makes SEC-PARAM-001 structural rather than validated -- there is no argument for a caller to lie in. Measured on the pinned pgvector:pg18 image across nine arms with the negative control run first (one expectation inverted produced DIVERGES and exit 1), every request made as the authenticator with SET ROLE because a privilege result measured as a superuser measures nothing (ADR 0065/0066): the hook's app.agent_id IS readable inside a VOLATILE SECURITY DEFINER function in the same transaction; an unset custom GUC reads as the EMPTY STRING and not NULL, which is why every read here is spelled nullif(current_setting(...), '') exactly as 0018 spells it; the definer inserts into a table the caller holds nothing on and whose schema it cannot even USE, while the same caller doing it directly is denied with 42501 and leaves zero rows -- the control without which the first arm would be about a table anybody can write. The decisive arm is D489: a write that RAISEs loses its audit row, because the RAISE aborts the transaction and the row inserted before it goes too. There is no arrangement of exception blocks or subtransactions that keeps it -- a handler discards its savepoint just as surely -- so a row written inside the transaction it describes can record a COMMITTED change and nothing else. That is why the table carries a `source` column: an agent_plane row records what was ATTEMPTED and sees the denials and failures that never reach this database, and a database row records what actually CHANGED and sees a write that reached PostgREST directly without going near the agent plane, which an agent token can do because that is how the plane forwards it (D480). Two enums rather than CHECK constraints, in app_private rather than api because nothing here is served: only an enum reaches the generated document (ADR 0058) and a CHECK passes when its expression is NULL (ADR 0080). api.create_note and api.update_task_status are replaced with CREATE OR REPLACE on the same signature so 0007's grants and 0005's REVOKEs survive, and their bodies were written from 0007's text rather than from memory of it (D270) -- the AP401 guard, the FOR UPDATE lock, the expected-status comparison and the AP404/AP409/AP422 contract are unchanged, and the diff is one conditional INSERT each, firing only when app.agent_id is set so a human caller is unaffected. agent_audit_complete is scoped to the calling agent's own rows and returns boolean rather than raising when nothing matched, so it cannot be used as an oracle for another agent's record ids, and it refuses the `committed` outcome because that belongs to a database row it does not write. The grants agent_writer never received are here (D475): grep -c agent_writer on 0018 returns ZERO, so the role held no USAGE on app_private and no EXECUTE on the hook or on either comparison helper, and a write token would have been refused by 'permission denied for function postgrest_pre_request' rather than by the boundary -- D417's shape one session later, in a migration whose own text already stated the rule that both comparison helpers go to every role that runs the hook, because role and token_use are independent claims and every combination is a reachable request. This migration grants privileges only; the authenticator's membership in agent_writer is GRANT role TO role, which is bootstrap plane (D102, D266) and is Run 2's, and this migration must land first because privileges granted to a role nothing can assume are inert while the reverse order produces a request that fails on the hook instead of on the boundary. mcp_audit_service receives nothing and is in no placeholder list: ADR 0135 decides it stays unactivated rather than deferring the question again, because the definer route needs no service identity. No request role holds SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on app_private.agent_audit; the definer functions are the only paths in, which is 0014's arrangement for the storage plane and ADR 0052's for the identity registry. Targeted REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION ... FROM PUBLIC beside each new function rather than the blanket form (D57, re-measured as D262), RESET ROLE below the privileges block (D285), and this is 0019 rather than an edit to 0018 or 0007 because two clusters hold both (ADR 0091). See ADR 0135, ADR 0052, ADR 0057, ADR 0091.

migrations.name: agent_audit_reader
migrations.description: The one reader of the audit record, and the grant that makes it reachable. app_private.auth_list_agent_audit is a STABLE SECURITY DEFINER function over app_private.agent_audit, granted to auth_service alone, and it is what GET /admin/audit sends behind the admin_audit:read scope. It exists as 0020 rather than as an edit to 0019 because 0019 is released and released migrations are fix-forward only (ADR 0091), and it exists at all because of D501: 0019 created the table and the two indexes whose own comment says they are for this reader -- 'The admin query endpoint (Run 7) reads by owner and by agent, most recent first' -- and created neither the reader nor a grant, so auth_service, which holds schema USAGE on app_private and nothing else, had no statement it was allowed to send. A definer function rather than a SELECT grant because the table's own COMMENT says no role holds SELECT on it and the definer functions are the only paths in, which is 0014's arrangement for the storage plane and ADR 0052's for the identity registry (ADR 0142). Both filters are optional and neither widens what the caller may see -- an administrator holding admin_audit:read may read the whole record -- so they narrow a permitted read rather than authorize one, which is a different question from SEC-PARAM-001 and is stated so the signature is not read as a counterexample to it. p_limit is applied and not clamped: the route validates the caller's limit into its documented range and answers 422 outside it, so a second bound here would be a second authority over one rule and the two would drift (D495, D463). The ORDER BY carries an id tiebreak because started_at defaults to now(), which is transaction time, so two rows from one transaction share it exactly and an arbitrary order under a LIMIT is a row that appears in no page. Granted to auth_service and to nobody else: not project_admin, whose scope is checked at the endpoint and which as a request role could otherwise reach the record over PostgREST with no scope check; not either agent role, because ADR 0135's stated threat is an agent adding noise under a true identity and reading the record back is not part of that; not api_documentation, because this function is not in api and granting it is the one thing that could change that. Targeted REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION ... FROM PUBLIC before the grant (D57, re-measured as D262), which takes nothing from a named grantee (D267) so the fourteen earlier grants to auth_service are not restated, and RESET ROLE below the privileges block (D285). No NOTIFY: nothing in api moved, and announcing a reload for a change PostgREST cannot see is a notification a later reader has to explain. This migration does NOT close D500 -- the database-source row still carries no request_id -- because that means replacing both write RPCs, which is a change to what the product writes rather than a way to read what is already written. See ADR 0142, ADR 0052, ADR 0091, ADR 0135.

migrations.name: agent_writer_context_grants
migrations.description: The two grants that make agent_writer an agent rather than only a writer, and it is D508. ADR 0118 decided the agent plane's RPCs are reviewed and unpublished -- REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC, granted to agent_reader alone -- and 0018 implemented that exactly, at a time when agent_reader was the only agent role. Session 9 activated a second one: 0019 gave agent_writer everything a WRITE needs (USAGE on app_private, EXECUTE on the pre-request hook, on both comparison helpers and on both audit functions) and its own comment quotes the count that made that omission visible, 'grep -c agent_writer on 0018 returns ZERO'. It asked that question of the write path and not of the agent path, so api.mcp_agent_context() kept the grant list ADR 0118 gave it. Measured on alpha-dev at release f3004fd as the role and never as a superuser (ADR 0065/0066), with agent_reader making the same call as the control without which 'permission denied' cannot be told from a function broken for everyone: as agent_writer, SELECT * FROM api.mcp_agent_context() is 'ERROR: permission denied for function mcp_agent_context'; as agent_reader the same statement returns 0 rows, having reached it. What that cost is every request and not every write: ADR 0125 resolves the caller's context once per request in on_request, before discovery and before execution, and mcp_agent_context is the statement it sends -- so a write agent was refused before its scope was checked, before its audit record was opened and before api.create_note was reached. That is why the Session 9 host gate answered 'upstream refused with status 403' on every write, why app_private.agent_audit held no row for any of them, and why PostgREST logged nothing: a 403 is not a 5xx at its level. api.owner_activity_report() is granted beside it because a repair aimed only at the observed failure would have left the next one hidden behind it: it backs the run_report capability whose required_scopes are [notes:read, tasks:read], both inside agent_writer's ceiling, so a write agent may hold them, discoverable_by will offer the tool, and the call would have been refused by the same missing grant one step further on. Nothing else changes: no new function, no new table, no widened ceiling, no third agent role, and agent_writer receives exactly what agent_reader already holds on these two functions. app_private.auth_list_agent_audit is deliberately not granted -- ADR 0142 gives the audit record one reader, auth_service, and an agent must not read the record that attributes it. No targeted REVOKE is restated: it takes nothing from a named grantee (D267). A NOTIFY is issued as a precaution rather than on a measurement, and the template says so: whether PostgREST's cache holds function privileges has not been measured here, and the asymmetry favours issuing it. This is 0021 rather than an edit to 0019 because 0019 and 0020 are released and applied on both clusters (ADR 0091). See ADR 0118, ADR 0125, ADR 0091.

migrations.name: database_row_request_id
migrations.description: The database-source audit row records the request that caused it, closing D500. One MCP write produces two audit rows -- an agent_plane row the runtime writes and a database row the RPC writes inside the transaction it describes -- and only the first carried a request_id, so the two correlated by agent, tool and time. This is 0022 rather than an edit to 0019 because 0019 is released and applied on both clusters (ADR 0091), and 0020's own comment set the terms: closing D500 means replacing both write RPCs, which is a change to what the product writes rather than a way to read what is already written, and the deployment test asserting the database row's request_id IS NULL stays green until the day the repair lands. It lands here, and that test is replaced by a stricter one in the same commit under ADR 0161. The value is the runtime's own mint and never a caller's (ADR 0160): the MCP plane stamps one id per HTTP request and forwards it upstream on every call, so the id arriving here is the same one Traefik logged as downstream_X-Request-Id on the way out -- four legs, one value. How the header reads was measured in Session 11 Run 1 through PostgREST at the pinned digest, through a role switch, behind a db-pre-request hook, inside a SECURITY DEFINER function with SET search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp (D632): the key is lowercase x-request-id, a capitalised lookup read NULL in the same request the lowercase one succeeded, an absent key is SQL NULL rather than the empty string so the repository's nullif(current_setting(...), '') idiom is deliberately not used, and the two-argument current_setting is required because these functions are reachable from psql where the GUC does not exist and the one-argument form raises. The value is guarded before it is cast, and D633 is why: an unguarded cast does not fail to correlate, it destroys the write. Measured, a function that inserts a row and then casts a malformed caller-supplied header raises 22P02, PostgREST answers 400, and the table is left with zero rows, while the well-formed control committed both rows in the same invocation and a missing header is harmless because NULL::uuid is NULL. Two existing decisions forbid the naive version so this makes no new one: ADR 0141 makes a write fail closed on ITS OWN audit record and a caller's malformed header is caller input rather than this deployment's record failing, and ADR 0139 requires a write refusal to be translated from the product's own PT errcode rather than relayed, which a raw 22P02 surfacing as 400 is not. A shape test rather than BEGIN ... EXCEPTION, because an exception block opens a subtransaction on every agent write and a regex is a comparison. app_private.agent_request_id() is one helper called by both RPCs rather than the expression written twice, which is question 5 answered in advance: a third write RPC added later gets the rule by calling it instead of getting whichever copy its author read, and D500 exists because 0019 asked a question of one path and not the other. It is STABLE, SECURITY INVOKER, REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC and granted to nobody -- it needs no privilege of its own and executes as the owner of the SECURITY DEFINER function that calls it. Both RPC signatures are unchanged, so nothing in api is created, dropped or re-signatured and no grant moves; the bodies are 0019's verbatim except for the one column added to each INSERT. A NOTIFY is issued for 0021's stated reason, on the same open question about what PostgREST's cache holds. The residual is stated in ADR 0161 rather than discovered later: a caller reaching PostgREST directly chooses the request_id on its own database row. It cannot forge agent_id or owner_id, which come from GUCs the pre-request hook set, so this is ADR 0135's conceded case of an agent adding noise to its own record, and the noise is visible because such a row still carries its own agent_id -- an operator correlating by request id should check agent_id beside it. See ADR 0161, ADR 0160, ADR 0141, ADR 0139, ADR 0091.
